case.believed: Axios request and response interceptors both run in registration order, every registered asynchronous request interceptor makes the whole request asynchronous even when runWhen skips it, and a rejected handler only catches errors from its own fulfilled handler.
contract: Request interceptors execute in last-registered-first order, while response interceptors execute in first-registered-first order.

When every selected request interceptor is marked synchronous, request interceptors and the adapter run before axios.get returns its Promise; an ordinary asynchronous interceptor defers the pipeline to a microtask.
runWhen is evaluated before pipeline construction, and an asynchronous interceptor skipped by runWhen does not force the remaining synchronous pipeline to become asynchronous.
eject removes one interceptor while preserving the others, and clear removes every interceptor from that manager.
A rejected handler on an older request interceptor catches an error thrown by a newer interceptor that executes before it, can return the saved config, and lets dispatch continue to the adapter.
case.goal: Prove Axios 1.19.0 request/response interceptor order, synchronous and runWhen scheduling, eject/clear removal, and rejected-handler recovery with an offline adapter.
